title: 50 mila lavoratori negli Emirati. Ecco come l’Etiopia riduce la disoccupazione
description: 50 mila lavoratori saranno inviati negli Emirati Arabi Uniti come parte di un programma per modernizzare la forza lavoro. Lo ha annunciato il primo ministro etiope Abiy Ahmed che in questo modo intende ridurre la disoccupazione nel suo paese. Il premier ha chiarito che, oltre a quelli già previsti, sono in corso negoziati per l'invio di 200 mila lavoratori in tre anni. E ci sarebbero alla finestra, come paesi destinatari, anche alcuni Stati europei e il Giappone. L’idea dell’esecutivo è che in tal modo gli etiopi potranno guadagnare salari migliori e saranno in grado di perfezionare le loro capacità, prima di ritornare ricchi di know-how nel proprio paese di origine. Sullo sfondo le relazioni geopolitiche tra i paesi dell’Africa orientale e quelli mediorientali. E, in particolare, tra Etiopia ed Emirati Arabi Uniti, che nel 2018 si sono impegnati a iniettare 2,6 miliardi di euro nelle casse etiopi. Una possibile parziale spiegazione dell’originale modo scelto dal paese africano per ridurre la disoccupazione.

Background The Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration (DDR) program for Ethiopia was initiated as a crucial step towards implementing the peace agreement signed between the Government of Ethiopia and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) on 2nd November 2022 in South Africa. This agreement ended the long-standing conflict that had arisen between the TPLF and the central government in Ethiopia, resulting in widespread violence and displacement. The objective of the DDR program is to facilitate the disarmament of former combatants from Tigray, Amhara and Afar, their demobilization and eventual reintegration into civilian life. The program is geared towards restoring peace, promoting reconciliation and creating a conducive environment for sustainable development. Eventual areas of coverage will go beyond Northern Ethiopia and cover other regions of Ethiopia. The Government of Ethiopia has mandated and created the “National Rehabilitation Commission (NRC)” which is responsible for design, planning, implementation, and monitoring of the DDR programme in the country. The overall DDR beneficiaries identified are 371,971. The Government has planned implementation of the programme. In Phase 1, a total of 75,000 combatants will be demobilized in 2024 and the balance will be demobilized in 2025. UNDP is supporting the NRC in close coordination with various national and international partners, including the United Nations, non-governmental organizations, and other actors. It is expected that the DDR program will provide an opportunity for the combatants in North Ethiopia to turn their focus towards peaceful and productive activities, thereby contributing to the overall stability and development of the North Ethiopia region. The DDR program has close linkages with the National Dialogue, Transitional Justice, and Peace Support programme. The DDR programme is anchored in the Governance Unit. title: International Expert Trainer
description: Expression of Interest- International Expert Trainer (IET) Opportunity Making the Transition to English (MTE) Project – Ethiopia Independent Trainer (Non-Permanent Worker – NPW) Assignment Location: Ethiopia (with some remote delivery from trainer’s home location) Contract Type: Consultancy Agreement (Independent Consultant/NPW) The closing date for applications is 14 August 2026 About The British Council The British Council is the UK’s international organisation for cultural relations and educational opportunities. We support peace and prosperity by building connections, understanding and trust between people in the UK and countries worldwide through education, the English language and the arts. About The Making The Transition To English (MTE) Programme The British Council is seeking expressions of interest from experienced teacher/teacher educator trainers to support the Making the Transition to English (MTE) Project in Ethiopia , funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). The project aims to support the Ethiopian Ministry of Education, Regional Education Bureaus and other education sector institutions in strengthening the transition to English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) for learners in Grades 7 and 8. The Project Will Focus On: Improving teachers’ English language proficiency. Strengthening teaching and learning practices. Developing sustainable teacher professional development systems. Building national capacity for continuous professional development (CPD). A Key Project Objective Is To Develop: 100 National Expert Trainers (NETs) who will become national teacher/teacher educator trainers. More than 7,000 Transformation Coaches who will train and support approximately 36,000 teachers across Ethiopia. To support this ambitious project, the British Council intends to engage the services of up to six International Expert Trainers (IETs). About The Training Assignment The International Expert Trainer (IET) will provide specialist training and materials development expertise in: English Language Teaching (ELT) Teacher professional development Teacher educator development Materials development Training programme design and delivery This is an independent training assignment and does not constitute employment with the British Council. Successful trainers will provide agreed consultancy services under a consultancy agreement and will be responsible for delivering defined outputs and professional services. This will involve being set up as a vendor on the British Council financial system. The assignment will follow a "Jet In – Jet Out" delivery model , combining: Scheduled in-country delivery periods on the ground in Ethiopia. Remote technical support and preparation activities from the trainer’s location. The duration, deployment schedule and level of input will be confirmed based on project requirements. Scope of Training Services The International Expert Trainer will provide expertise across the following areas: Professional Development Design The Trainer Will: Design and develop professional development resources for National Expert Trainers. Adapt existing British Council and Ministry of Education materials. Create additional learning resources aligned with programme objectives. Support the development of sustainable training approaches. Technical Advisory Support The trainer will provide specialist advice and technical input to: National Expert Trainers Transformation Coaches Other education sector stakeholders if/when required Areas Of Advice May Include: Supporting the transition to EMI Teacher and teacher educator development approaches. Teacher educator competency frameworks. Training programme design and implementation Training Delivery and Facilitation The Trainer Will: Deliver/Co-deliver intensive face-to-face National Expert Trainer training programmes in Ethiopia. Deliver virtual workshops, technical sessions and other training activities as required. Support additional collaborative professional development activities. Provide coaching and developmental feedback to the National Expert Trainers and other project participants if/when required. Capacity Strengthening The Trainer Will Support National Expert Trainers To: Design effective training programmes. Develop facilitation skills. Mentor and support Transformation Coaches. Improve training delivery through observation and feedback. Build sustainable national training capacity. Monitoring, Reporting and Knowledge Sharing The Trainer Will: Support monitoring, evaluation and learning activities. Participate in programme review meetings when required. Essential Qualifications Applicants must demonstrate: A university degree or equivalent qualification. Cambridge DELTA or equivalent recognised ELT diploma level qualification. title: Anesthesiologist critical care
description: Company Description Debre Berhan University is a public higher education institution committed to advancing teaching, research, and community service. The university focuses on developing skilled professionals who can contribute to national and regional health systems. Its medical and health sciences programs emphasize evidence-based practice, ethical care, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Debre Berhan University provides an academic environment where clinicians, educators, and researchers work together to improve patient outcomes and strengthen healthcare delivery. Role Description This is a full-time, on-site Anesthesiologist Critical Care role based in Debre Birhan. The role involves providing perioperative anesthesia care, managing critically ill patients in intensive care settings, and supporting surgical teams during complex procedures. Daily tasks include preoperative assessment, administering anesthesia, monitoring patients during and after surgery, and overseeing pain management plans. The anesthesiologist will collaborate with surgeons, critical care nurses, and other clinicians to stabilize patients with life-threatening conditions, participate in multidisciplinary rounds, and ensure adherence to clinical protocols and safety standards. The role may also include teaching medical learners and contributing to quality improvement and clinical research within the university hospital. Qualifications Strong foundation in Anesthesiology and Medicine, with demonstrated ability to manage perioperative and critical care cases. Experience collaborating with Critical Care Nursing professionals in intensive care units to deliver coordinated patient care. Clinical exposure to Surgery, including support for major and emergency procedures in an operating room environment. Competence in Pain Management, including acute and postoperative pain control and use of multimodal analgesia. Medical degree (MD or equivalent) and specialized training or residency in Anesthesiology; board certification or eligibility is preferred. Experience in critical care settings, including ventilator management, hemodynamic monitoring, and resuscitation. Commitment to patient safety, ethical practice, continuous learning, and evidence-based medicine. Strong communication, teamwork, and teaching skills, with the ability to work effectively in a diverse academic and clinical environment.

Request for Proposal Prequalification of Printing, Branding and Production Service Providers Ethiopia Framework Agreement (2026 – 2028) July 2026 Procurement Summary Item Description Client Girl Effect Ethiopia Assignment Prequalification of Printing, Branding & Production Service Providers Procurement Method Open Competitive Procurement Contract Type Framework Agreement Framework Period September 2026 – August 2028 Number of Suppliers Multiple suppliers may be appointed Location Ethiopia Currency Ethiopian Birr (ETB) Who We Are Girl Effect is an international non-profit organisation that creates media, technology and behaviour change programmes that empower adolescent girls and young people to improve their health, education and economic opportunities. In Ethiopia, Girl Effect delivers programmes through the Yegna youth brand, reaching millions of young people through media, digital platforms, community engagement and research. These programmes require a wide range of professionally produced printing, branding and promotional materials to support programme implementation across Ethiopia Objective Girl Effect Ethiopia seeks to establish a roster of qualified printing, branding and production service providers for a two-year Framework Agreement. Suppliers appointed to the framework may be invited to participate in: Restricted Requests for Quotations (RFQs) Mini-competitions Direct call-off assignments depending on the nature, value and complexity of future requirements. Appointment to the framework does not guarantee any minimum volume of work. Framework Period The framework agreement shall remain valid for: September 2026 –August 2028 Girl Effect reserves the right to extend the framework for an additional period, subject to satisfactory performance. What You’ll Do The selected suppliers shall be capable of providing one or more of the following services: A. Programme and Educational Materials Student Manuals /Facilitator Guides – Booklets - 60 pages Size: A5 Portrait (unless otherwise specified) Printing: Full colour (CMYK), double-sided Inside Pages: 150 GSM white bond paper, glossy Cover: 300 gsm art card with matte or gloss lamination Binding: Saddle stitched or perfect bound depending on page count Finish: Trimmed and neatly finished Discussion Guides – Flip Charts - 20 pages Size: A3 Landscape (297 × 420 mm) Printing: Full colour, double-sided Paper: 250 gsm art card, glossy Mounting: White laminated rigid board backing Type: Self-standing flip chart Finish: Durable and suitable for repeated use during training sessions Conversation Card - Flash Cards Size: A5 or A6 (as specified) Printing: Full colour, double-sided Material: 300 gsm art card Finish: Matte or gloss lamination with rounded corners where required Fact Sheets - Brochure Size: A4 or A3 folded Printing: Full colour, double-sided Paper: 170 gsm art paper Finish: Folded and neatly trimmed B. Information, Education and Communication Materials Posters Sizes: A3, A2, A1 or custom sizes Printing: Full colour, single or double-sided Paper: 200 gsm art paper Finish: Matte or gloss finish as required Flyers Size: A5 or DL Printing: Full colour, double-sided Paper: 150 gsm art paper Finish: Trimmed and bundled Leaflets Size: A4 folded to DL or A5 Printing: Full colour Paper: 150–170 gsm art paper Finish: Bi-fold or tri-fold as required Brochures Size: A4 folded (Bi-fold or Tri-fold) Printing: Full colour Paper: 170 gsm art paper Finish: Professionally folded Calendars Type: Wall or Desk Calendar Printing: Full colour Cover: 300 gsm art card Inside Pages: 170–200 gsm art paper Binding: Wire binding with hanging hook where applicable Stickers Material: Vinyl or self-adhesive paper Printing: Full colour Finish: Gloss laminated Cutting: Die-cut or kiss-cut depending on design C. Event and Activation Materials Roll-up Banners Size: 85 × 200 cm Material: Premium anti-curl banner material Printing: Full colour Includes: Aluminium stand and carrying bag Backdrops Material: 440 gsm PVC Flex or fabric Printing: Full colour Finish: Hemmed edges with eyelets Stage Branding Material: PVC Flex, fabric or foam board depending on requirement Printing: Full colour Installation: Where requested Directional Signage Material: Foam board, PVC board or Sunboard Printing: Full colour Finish: Mounted where applicable Event Badges Material: PVC card or laminated art card Printing: Full colour Includes: Lanyard where required Certificates Size: A4 Printing: Full colour Paper: 300 gsm ivory or art card Finish: Matte or gloss finish D. Branding and Promotional Materials Branded Notebooks Size: A5 or A4 Cover: 300 gsm laminated art card or hard cover Inside Pages: 80 gsm ruled or plain paper Binding: Spiral or perfect bound Branded Folders Size: A4 Material: 350 gsm art card Finish: Matte or gloss lamination Features: Business card slot and document pocket Branded Pens Plastic or metal body Single or multi-colour branding Screen printing or UV printing Branded Tote Bags Material: Heavy-duty canvas or cotton Printing: Screen printing, heat transfer or DTF printing Colour: As specified T-Shirts Material: 100% cotton (180–200 gsm) Printing: Screen printing, DTF or embroidery Sizes: Small to XXL Polo Shirts Material: Cotton pique (220 gsm) Branding: Embroidery or high-quality printing Sizes: Small to XXL Caps Material: Cotton twill Branding: Embroidery or screen printing Adjustable fastening Lanyards Material: Polyester Printing: Full-colour sublimation Includes: Metal hook and safety buckle where required Water Bottles Material: Aluminium or stainless steel Branding: UV print, screen print or laser engraving Mugs Material: Ceramic Branding: Sublimation printing Capacity: Approximately 330 ml Wristbands Material: Silicone or fabric Branding: Printed or embossed logo Promotional Merchandise Suppliers should also be able to provide other branded promotional items, including but not limited to umbrellas, key holders, USB drives, notebooks, desk accessories, gift sets, and corporate giveaways. E. Office and Corporate Materials Business Cards Size: 85 × 55 mm Printing: Full colour, double-sided Paper: 350 gsm art card Finish: Matte or gloss lamination Letterheads Size: A4 Printing: Full colour Paper: 100 gsm bond paper Compliment Slips Size: DL Printing: Full colour Paper: 120 gsm bond paper Envelopes Sizes: DL, A5 and A4 Printing: Single or full colour Paper: 100–120 gsm bond paper Note: Suppliers should demonstrate capability to print materials in: Amharic, Afan Oromo, Sidamic, Afar, Somali, Tigrinya, English and other Ethiopian languages where required. Procurement Timelines Terms of Reference Published : July 29, 2026 Deadline for Proposal Submission : August 20, 2026 Supplier Eligibility Requirements Interested suppliers must submit: Company Documentation Valid Business License Certificate of Incorporation/Registration TIN Registration Certificate VAT Registration Certificate Valid Tax Clearance Certificate Company Profile Technical Capacity Description of printing facilities List of printing equipment List of finishing equipment Production capacity per day/week Quality assurance procedures Relevant Experience Minimum three years' experience providing printing services At least three references from similar assignments Portfolio of completed work Financial Capacity Audited financial statements (last two years) or equivalent financial records Bank reference letter Proposal Submission Requirements Technical Proposal The technical proposal should include: Company Overview Company profile Years in operation Areas of specialization Relevant Experience Similar assignments undertaken NGO, donor or development sector experience Production Capacity Printing technology available Production capability Staffing structure Quality Management Quality assurance processes Sample approval procedures Reprint and defect management processes Delivery and Logistics Delivery capability Geographic coverage Turnaround times Sample Submission Suppliers should submit at least three examples of recently completed print assignments demonstrating: Colour quality Binding quality Finishing quality Branding execution Durability Financial Proposal The Financial Proposal in Ethiopian shall be submitted separately from the Technical Proposal using the Girl Effect Pricing Schedule . The Pricing Schedule has been designed to ensure a consistent and comparable evaluation of all submissions. Suppliers are requested to complete all applicable sections of the template and return it in its original Excel format. The completed pricing schedule should include, where applicable: Unit rates for all requested printing and production items. VAT and other applicable taxes. Delivery and transportation charges. Installation costs (where applicable). Minimum order quantities (where applicable). Standard production lead times. Bulk order discounts. Any additional charges or assumptions. Price validity period. Where a particular item or service is not offered, suppliers should indicate "Not Applicable (N/A)" within the template rather than deleting rows. Suppliers should not alter the structure or formulas contained within the pricing schedule unless specifically instructed by Girl Effect. The completed Financial Proposal template should be submitted together with the Technical Proposal by the submission deadline. Evaluation Criteria Relevant Experience 25% Technical Capacity 25% Quality Assurance & Samples 20% Delivery & Logistics Capability 10% Financial Competitiveness 15% References 5% Framework Management Girl Effect reserves the right to: Appoint multiple suppliers to the framework. Allocate suppliers by service category where appropriate. Conduct restricted RFQs or mini-competitions amongst prequalified suppliers. Issue direct call-off purchase orders where appropriate. Review supplier performance annually. Suspend or remove suppliers based on performance or compliance. Extend the framework period subject to satisfactory performance. Commercial and General Terms This procurement is intended to establish a non-exclusive framework agreement with multiple suppliers. Appointment to the framework does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work. Suppliers are responsible for ensuring compliance with Ethiopian tax legislation. All taxes should be clearly identified in the financial proposal. All materials developed under any subsequent call-off assignment shall become the property of Girl Effect unless otherwise agreed in writing. Successful suppliers will be required to comply with Girl Effect's safeguarding policies and may be required to undergo safeguarding checks before contract award. Girl Effect reserves the right to amend, suspend or cancel this procurement process at any stage and is not liable for any costs incurred by suppliers during the preparation or submission of proposals.

How to Apply: To apply for this opportunity, please submit a proposal by email with the subject line “**Prequalification of Printing, Branding and Production Service Providers – Ethiopia (2026–2028)** ” to **suppliers@girleffect.org** by August 20, 2026. For any questions, please also send them to our suppliers' email address.

title: Mine Action Specialist
description:
Overview of position General Background Our client supports the successful implementation of its partners’ peacebuilding, humanitarian and development projects around the world. Our mission is to serve people in need by expanding the ability of the United Nations, governments and other partners to manage projects, infrastructure and procurement in a sustainable and efficient manner. Working in some of the world’s most challenging environments, our vision is to advance sustainable implementation practices, always satisfying or surpassing our partners’ expectations. With over 7,000 personnel spread across 80 countries, our client offers its partners the logistical, technical and management knowledge they need, wherever they need it. A flexible structure and global reach mean that we can quickly respond to our partners' needs, while offering the benefits of economies of scale. Please provide general background information on the context of the engagement. Background Information - Peace and Security Cluster For over 20 years, our clients Peace and Security Cluster (PSC) has served as a key implementation platform supporting the work of its largest partner. Through a strategic partnership, PSC delivers interlinked portfolio, programme and project management services, reinforced by robust oversight and risk management controls tailored to operations in complex and high-risk environments. Operating under the leadership of the Cluster Director - who holds overall authority and accountability for PSC’s performance on behalf of its clients - the Cluster provides day-to-day management of their partners field programmes. This includes comprehensive support across human resources, procurement, contract management, planning, implementation, and financial oversight, ensuring full compliance with our client rules and regulations and donor requirements. PSC’s service delivery is complemented by cross-cutting initiatives, including knowledge and information management, gender equality, diversity and inclusion and quality assurance. The Cluster enables agile deployment and operational flexibility, allowing field programmes to respond swiftly to shifting needs in dynamic operational contexts. It also plays an essential role in donor reporting and visibility, ensuring that funding is used transparently and effectively. Background Information Established in 1997, our clients partner works to eliminate the threat of landmines, explosive remnants of war (ERW), and improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Their partner leads operational responses, coordinates mine action across the UN system, and contributes to global standards and policy development. They supports the UN's vision of "a world free of the threat of landmines and unexploded ordnance, where individuals and communities live in a safe environment conducive to development, and where mine survivors are fully integrated into their societies." Operating under mandates from both the UN General Assembly and Security Council, their functions as a specialized service within the Department of Peace Operations (DPO). They operates under UN legislative mandates of both the General Assembly and the Security Council, or at the request of the UN Secretary-General or his designated official. When instructed by the Security Council or called upon by Member States, their partner deploys under humanitarian, peace and security mandates. Their main headquarters is in the UN Secretariat, New York with a sub-office in Geneva. They provides direct support and assistance in the areas of explosive hazard threat mitigation to 18 countries/territories/missions, has a standby rapid response capacity and global technical advisors in the field of IEDs and Weapons and Ammunition Management. As an office within DPO, their partner supports peacekeeping and special political missions in accordance with Security Council mandates. They chair the Inter-Agency Coordination Group on Mine Action (IACG-MA) and leads the Mine Action Area of Responsibility under the Global Protection Cluster. It also chairs the IMAS Review Board and leads the UN Coordinating Task Force on IEDs, supporting the Secretary-General’s Disarmament Agenda. Background Information - Sudan The Sudan Programme, based in Port Sudan, works in close coordination with the National Mine Action Authority (NMAA), the UN Country Team and humanitarian partners. The project aims to protect civilians from the threat of explosive ordnance (EO) and strengthen the resilience of conflict-affected communities through a comprehensive, gender-mainstreamed and conflict-sensitive mine action response. It also supports broader humanitarian, early recovery and stabilization efforts by enabling safe access to areas contaminated by EO. Their Sudan’s key activities include land release operations, including urban EOD activities and building clearance, with the operational focus expected to shift toward the clearance of AT mines, including minimum-metal variants; delivery of both direct and indirect Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE), tailored to different gender and age groups; and provision of technical advice to humanitarian, development, and peacebuilding (HDP) actors to help them safely operate in EO-affected environments. The project also leads the coordination of the Mine Action Area of Responsibility (MA AoR) in Sudan, co-chairing the sector under the Global Protection Cluster framework. Through this role, their partner ensures that mine action is effectively integrated into humanitarian coordination mechanisms and that EO threats are adequately understood and addressed at all levels. While the Programme’s current operational footprint is primarily focused on areas under the control of the Sudan Government - especially urban areas in Khartoum and Al Jazirah - Sudan aspires to expand its outreach to all EO-affected regions, addressing both legacy contamination and new threats emerging from the ongoing conflict. Role objectives Under the direct supervision of the Head of Project Unit / Chief of Operations (HPU/CoO) or its representative, the Mine Action Specialist will perform the following tasks: Operations – Design and planning Support in providing input to the HPU or its representative on programme and project design documents from an operational and technical standpoint, such as: Workplan (e.g., nature of the threat, technical personnel and equipment requirements, etc.) Concept of Operations Input into the documents above is from the operational and technical aspects encompassing mine action pillars (e.g., clearance, explosive ordnance disposal, explosive ordnance risk education, victim assistance, advocacy, and stockpile destruction) Ensure that implementation plans have viable timelines, are assigned appropriate resources, and that implementation options reflect the knowledge of the context, as well as mechanisms and policies; key implementation documents include: Our clients Project Agreements Solicitation documents used to contract third parties (i.e., contractors and grantees) Human resources plan Support the design and planning of the national concept of operations and workplan, providing technical input to help ensure alignment with applicable standards, priorities and operational requirements. Operations - Implementation and monitoring Support and participate in the technical reviews to ensure operations are conducted in accordance with our clients policies and both International and National Mine Action standards, such as: Project management standards, Health, safety, social and environmental standards, Gender parity and mainstreaming policies, Ethics and standards of conduct, Information management systems and standards and Organizational design standards and human resources policies; Where applicable, in collaboration with the NMAC and as tasked, conduct routine on-site QA of Mine Action Organization operations (for monitoring and post-clearance inspections) and as part of the Accreditation process to ensure operations are conducted in accordance with mine action technical standards, such as: International and National Mine Action Standards (IMAS) and corresponding National Technical Specifications and Guidelines (NTSGs); Oversee, coordinate, and monitor mine action operations and performance (both operations conducted in-house and those conducted through third-party contractors and grantees). Ensure third-party contracts and grants are delivered in accordance with mine action technical, operational and quality assurance processes (Implementation Plan, SOPs, task orders issuance, accreditation). Implement the program quality management and information management system. Familiarize with and, when required, deliver EO-related courses, including SSAFE. Advise the HPU or its representative and the NMAC CoO on potential technical and operational issues that may impact the achievement of programme/project outcomes and appropriate solutions. Ensure operational plans are updated and reviewed regularly. Monitor and react to emerging trends in Land Release activities. Capacity Building & Mentorship Act as a mentor and training officer for the NMAC, providing guidance and support in operational implementation, operations management and field-level programme delivery in line with the NMAC-established priorities Develop training plans in conjunction with the HPU / CoO based on NMAC and MA Programme requirements and deliver training courses as necessary or when requested by the NMAC. Support the continuous improvement of operational practices by reviewing and updating of key documents, including Standards, Technical Guidelines, SOPs and Working practices and instructions (WPIs), in coordination with relevant stakeholders. Stakeholder management In support of the HPU or its representative, manage relationships with key stakeholders around operational and technical issues. Upon request from the HPU or its representative, engage national mine action authorities and/or relevant Government ministries for purposes of coordination. People management Mentor and advise NMAC and mine action operations personnel in planning, execution and delivery of allocated projects, ensuring incorporation of best operational processes. Promote teamwork, collaboration, and diversity by providing the Operations team with clear direction, objectives, and guidance to enable them to perform their duties responsibly, effectively, and efficiently. Foster a positive and enabling work environment, respectful of both men and women, and ensure that the highest standards of conduct are observed. Knowledge management and innovation Ensure records of operations-related files are well maintained. Effectively manage efficient and effective operations in their AOR. Keep abreast of and incorporate the latest/best practices, approaches, and technology to enhance operational results. Support e alignment of best practices and IM approaches between the NMAC. Impact of Results The MA Specialist’s effective and successful performance directly impacts the achievement of the project deliverables and mine action programme results and consequently reinforces the programme's visibility and image as well as the wider Mine Action Sector in Sudan. Project reporting Reporting on a weekly, monthly, and quarterly basis on progress to the Head of Project Unit (HPU) Ensure all reports are duly submitted and recorded in UNMAS database Key competencies An Advanced University Degree (Master’s Degree or equivalent) with a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience; or A First Level University Degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) with a minimum of 7 years of relevant experience; or A Secondary School Degree (High School of equivalent) with a minimum of 11 years of relevant experience is required. A recognised EOD Level 3 qualification is required. Preference will be given to candidates holding the IMAS Level 3+ Bulk Demolitions competency, or an equivalent nationally or organisationally recognised qualification demonstrating competence in the planning, management and conduct of bulk demolition operations. Relevant experience is defined as experience in project management in a military, humanitarian, conflict, post-conflict, or development context. A minimum of 5 years of proven and applicable experience (within the last ten years) in the conduct and management of Mine Action operations and, in particular, previous experience managing/implementing the following activities such as Explosive Ordnance Disposal, including multiple items and logistical demolitions, Non-technical survey, Technical survey, Manual mine clearance, including Road Clearance, Battle Area Clearance, Proven experience in designing and delivering training and mentorship is required (in humanitarian mine action or military or police settings), Experience in mentoring and coaching national counterparts in all core areas of mine action is required. Experience in conducting structured training and on-the-job instruction aligned with their required technical competencies is required. Training should be tailored to the needs of NMAC personnel and support their operational planning, management and field-level programme delivery. Knowledge of information management systems such as the Information Management System for Mine Action (IMSMA) is desired. Strategic Perspective - Develops and implements sustainable business strategies, thinks long term and externally in order to positively shape the organization. Anticipates and perceives the impact and implications of future decisions and activities on other parts of the organization. (For levels IICA-3 and above) Integrity and Inclusion - Treats all individuals with respect; responds sensitively to differences and encourages others to do the same. Upholds organizational and ethical norms. Maintains high standards of trustworthiness. Role model for diversity and inclusion. Leading Self and Others - Acts as a positive role model contributing to the team spirit. Collaborates and supports the development of others. For people managers only: Acts as positive leadership role model, motivates, directs and inspires others to succeed, utilizing appropriate leadership styles. Partnering - Demonstrates understanding of the impact of own role on all partners and always puts the end beneficiary first. Builds and maintains strong external relationships and is a competent partner for others (if relevant to the role). Results Orientation - Efficiently establishes an appropriate course of action for self and/or others to accomplish a goal. Actions lead to total task accomplishment through concern for quality in all areas. Sees opportunities and takes the initiative to act on them. Understands that responsible use of resources maximizes our impact on our beneficiaries. Agility - Open to change and flexible in a fast-paced environment. Effectively adapts own approach to suit changing circumstances or requirements. Reflects on experiences and modifies own behavior. Performance is consistent, even under pressure. Always pursues continuous improvements. Solutions Focused - Evaluates data and courses of action to reach logical, pragmatic decisions. Takes an unbiased, rational approach with calculated risks. Applies innovation and creativity to problem-solving. Effective Communication - Expresses ideas or facts in a clear, concise and open manner. Communication indicates a consideration for the feelings and needs of others. Actively listens and proactively shares knowledge. Handles conflict effectively, by overcoming differences of opinion and finding common ground. Fluency in English language (Reading, writing, speaking) is required Fluency in any other UN official language (Reading, writing, speaking) is desired. Team management Mentor and advise NMAC and UNMAS operations personnel in planning, execution, and delivery of allocated projects, ensuring incorporation of best operational processes. Promote teamwork, collaboration, and diversity by providing the Operations team with clear direction, objectives, and guidance to enable them to perform their duties responsibly, effectively, and efficiently. Foster a positive and enabling work environment, respectful of both men and women, and ensure that the highest standards of conduct are observed. Further information Candidates who do not hold an IMAS Level 3+ Bulk Demolitions qualification but possess an EOD Level 3 qualification must provide documented evidence of relevant operational experience in planning and conducting bulk demolitions. Such evidence may include operational logs, post-task reports, training records, or other verifiable documentation. Copies of all relevant qualifications and supporting documentation must be submitted as part of the application. EOD qualifications must have been issued by organisations that train and certify EOD personnel in accordance with IMAS Test and Evaluation Protocol (TEP) 09.30/01/2022. Applicants are responsible for providing evidence that their qualifications meet this requirement. Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.

title: Ethiopia Government Relations and Program Support Coordinator (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role One Acre Fund Ethiopia is seeking a Government Relations (GR) & Program Support Coordinator who will serve as the primary point of contact for the Zonal and Woreda Offices of Agriculture, as well as other government officials and external partners across Hadiya and Kembata Zones. The Coordinator will play a key role in strengthening these partnerships and supporting the establishment and expansion of One Acre Fund's program in the Central Ethiopia region. The GR and Program Support Coordinator will also play a key role in de-risking our field engagements through active information gathering, staff training, and compliance management to ensure that our operations can run smoothly with reduced disruptions and risks to our staff and farmers alike. As such, this role is critical to the success of the program. The GR and Program Support Coordinator based in Hosaena town will be a key deputy to the One Acre Fund’s Senior Partnerships Associate based in Addis Ababa. Responsibilities Manage work relationships with woreda government and Zonal Focal Persons (FPs) Serve as the primary day-to-day liaison with woreda and zonal project focal persons (FP) and other government stakeholders. Over time, take on increasing responsibility for managing relationships with regional government institutions and supporting broader government engagement across the region. Proactively identify stakeholder issues at the woreda and kebele levels by maintaining close communication with the program team, particularly Tree Officers (TOs) and Cluster Leads (CLs), and work with relevant government stakeholders to resolve them in a timely manner. Participate in the weekly cluster lead meetings to understand GR challenges that may exist in the field and resolve them on time by leveraging run alignment meetings with woreda and zonal FPs as needed Attend other government meetings as directed by the Senior Partnerships Associate Leverage networks and knowledge of the landscape to help identify opportunities to expand and/or improve One Acre Fund’s work Prepare, organize, review, and submit documents as required on time to project signatory offices and other government offices, especially quarterly reports Gather inputs for quarterly reports from department leads or their designee Write and develop clear and concise quarterly reports that track progress and inform project stakeholders. Coordinate the review from his manager, incorporate comments, and finalize the report. Coordinate the submission of the reports to the woreda, zone and regional project signatory offices. Prepare project mid-term and terminal reports. Prepare outgoing letters for woredas as needed. Identify, monitor, and obtain all compliance requirements at the woreda and zonal government level and submit documents as required. Track woreda FPs’ and DAs’ support to OAF activities and field staff on a weekly basis, evaluate results, and take appropriate actions to increase program efficiency Monitor the assistance provided by woreda FPs and DAs to OAF operations on a weekly basis using a tracker Evaluate results and resolve issues in consultation with Woreda SHs and zonal focal persons. Ensure that the woreda FPs and DAs are fulfilling their roles and responsibilities as per prior agreements with One Acre Fund Participate in the resolution of identified issues/risks with manager support. Troubleshooting of Woreda Government Relations in consultation with the Senior Partnerships Specialist and with escalation, Organize and lead meetings and trainings as needed with support from your manager Provide GR capacity-building trainings to field team at least once a year Support on GR orientation and onboarding of new Woreda and Kebele employees, Co-lead project launch, mid-term, and terminal workshops Support/facilitate field visits and events for external stakeholders. Provide other administrative support as needed Other Projects Other Partnerships and Program projects as assigned by your supervisor (when time and skill allow) Special projects in the first year might include things like data entry, translating documents into Amharic, scanning and binding of documents, support on inventory, support during input distributions, and support during seedling distribution. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: University degree Minimum three years of work experience, withOne year of partnerships or communications work experience Worked and lived in the Central Ethiopia region for at least two years Independently facilitated and organized a workshop Some public speaking with training delivery, or teaching experience Very good report writing skills Excellent communication and social skills Excellent attention to details Willingness to travel via public transport to remote kebeles Good problem-solving skills and ability to learn quickly Challenge anticipation skills Good computer skills—in email, Excel and Word Fluent in English, Amharic, Hadiyegna and Keffagna (both written and spoken Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Hosaena Town, Ethiopia Benefits Health insurance, paid time off Contract Duration 1 year Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Ethiopia. Application Deadline 20 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @ oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here ( globalhotline@oneacrefund.org ), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

title: Information Management Intern
description:
Organization 3iS is an international non-profit organization that provides information management services to humanitarian and development organizations. 3iS has been working in Ethiopia since 2018, supporting humanitarian partners to improve information management and analysis for decision-making. Scope of Work 3iS is seeking an Information Management (IM) Intern to support humanitarian data management, visualization, and reporting efforts. This position provides an excellent opportunity for a motivated individual to gain hands-on experience in information management, data analysis, and the design of information products. The intern will assist the IM team in creating tools, reports, and visuals to support evidence-based decision-making across projects. Main Responsibilities 1. Data Management - Assist in collecting, cleaning, and consolidating data from various sources. - Support the design and maintenance of databases, spreadsheets, and other data tools. - Ensure the quality and consistency of data for analysis and reporting. 2. Visualization and Reporting - Support the production of high-quality infographics, charts, and dashboards to visualize project data. - Assist in the creation of interactive data products and reports, ensuring clarity and alignment with 3iS branding. - Help design periodic situation reports, factsheets, and summary visuals based on project data. 3. Mapping - Assist in producing basic maps using GIS tools (e.g., QGIS or ArcGIS) for data visualization and reporting purposes. - Support the team with geographic data organization and processing. 4. Needs Assessments and Analysis - Help organize and process data for needs assessments and analysis activities. - Support the preparation of presentation materials and reports summarizing key findings. 5. Capacity Building Support - Assist in preparing training materials and content for IM training sessions. - Support virtual or in-person IM workshops as needed, including note-taking and preparation of materials. Qualifications and Experience Education Enrolled in or recently completed a degree in Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Geography, Computer Science, GIS, or related fields. Technical Skills - Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and basic data analysis tools. - Familiarity with data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau, or Canva) is a strong advantage. - Basic knowledge of GIS tools (e.g., QGIS, ArcGIS) is desirable. - Knowledge of tools like KoboToolbox, Open Data Kit (ODK), or similar platforms is an asset. - Interest in learning and applying artificial intelligence tools to enhance data analysis, reporting, and visualization workflows. Competency - Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain data quality. - Good organizational skills and ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. - Ability to work effectively as part of a team. - Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. About DRC   
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is an international humanitarian organization with operations in 40 countries dedicated to assisting, protecting, and finding solutions for refugees, internally displaced and other conflict-affected communities. To stay relevant and meet the needs of the people we serve, we are exploring new, innovative ways of responding to displacement crises.   
 For the past years, DRC has increasingly engaged in anticipatory action for both climate- and conflict-induced displacement. We have developed innovative tools to forecast displacement from hazards to enable humanitarian actors to get ahead of crises. In East Africa and the Great Lakes region, DRC’s AA portfolio currently encompasses five countries and expanding regional partnerships with the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and leading agencies within the AA community of practice

Overall purpose of the role: 
The Danish Refugee Council is looking for a highly experienced Global Anticipatory Action (AA) Coordinator to provide technical leadership over an assigned anticipatory action portfolio covering countries in East Africa and the Great Lakes. After identifying convergence zones, UNHCR is working to mobilize development and peace actors to carry out stabilization and development activities aimed at empowering the population. Who We Are

Girl Effect is an international non-profit organisation that creates media, technology and behaviour change programmes that empower adolescent girls and young people to improve their health, education and economic opportunities.

In Ethiopia, Girl Effect delivers programmes through the Yegna youth brand, reaching millions of young people through media, digital platforms, community engagement and research. Objective

Company Overview

Delivery and Logistics

  • Colour quality

The Financial Proposal in Ethiopian shall be submitted separately from the Technical Proposal using the Girl Effect Pricing Schedule.

The Pricing Schedule has been designed to ensure a consistent and comparable evaluation of all submissions. Suppliers are requested to complete all applicable sections of the template and return it in its original Excel format.

The completed pricing schedule should include, where applicable:

  • Installation costs (where applicable).

  • Bulk order discounts.

Where a particular item or service is not offered, suppliers should indicate "Not Applicable (N/A)" within the template rather than deleting rows.

Suppliers should not alter the structure or formulas contained within the pricing schedule unless specifically instructed by Girl Effect.

  • Technical Capacity 25%
  • Quality Assurance & Samples 20%

For any questions, please also send them to our suppliers email address.

  • All materials developed under any subsequent call-off assignment shall become the property of Girl Effect unless otherwise agreed in writing.

title: Ethiopia Chief of Staff
description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africas farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.

To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable.

The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1,500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa, and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices.

About the Role

The Chief of Staff acts as a strategic and execution partner to the Country Director, ensuring strong people operations, internal systems, and cross-functional initiatives that enable the country program to deliver on its strategy.

The role combines line management of enabling functions (People Operations, HSS, Communications) with leadership of high-priority, cross-functional initiatives at the country level.

The Chief of Staff ensures clarity of priorities, clarity of execution, and effective coordination across teams, allowing the Country Director to focus on strategy, external relationships, and organizational leadership.

As Chief of Staff, you will work at the intersection of people systems, internal operations, and inter-departmental coordination:

  • You will lead the People Division by managing the People Operations, Finance admin, and Corporate Operations team, as well as the Communication and Health, Safety, and Security (HSS) teams.
  • You will lead implementation on important initiatives related to risk, compliance, team culture, and communication, as well as other cross-functional initiatives.
  • You will support the Country Director with briefs and internal reviews.

This role does not replace specialized HR technical functions; it focuses on leadership, integration, prioritization, and culture, with technical execution led by the People Operations team and global support functions.

Responsibilities

People Operations, HSS, and Communications Leadership

  • Manage the People Operations Lead (managing HR admin, Finance admin, compliance, and Corporate Operations), HSS team, and Communication team, ensuring:
    • Clear goals, accountability, and performance management
    • Strong delivery on core administrative, compliance, and support functions
    • High-quality HR administration, policies, and compliance
    • Continuous improvement of systems, processes, and staff experience
    • Support the People Operations Lead in driving improvement projects within the people function (e.g., onboarding, performance management, staff engagement)
  • Provide senior oversight of HR risk and employee relations
  • Act as country-level owner for organizational culture and people experience, including:
    • Strengthening a healthy, inclusive, and high-performance culture
    • Advancing Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) priorities at the country level
    • Monitor staff satisfaction and strengthen the use of data to drive HR performance
  • Act as country-level coordinator for talent and development priorities, including:
    • Overseeing country-level learning and development (L&D) priorities and annual plans
    • Partnering with department heads to support long-term staff development and career pathways
  • Ensure HSS systems effectively support staff safety, risk management, and duty of care
  • Ensure Communications supports country priorities, internal alignment, and external messaging, including planning staff retreats and internal events; managing company-wide communication

Cross-Functional Initiative Leadership (Country Priorities)

  • Lead high-priority cross-functional initiatives on behalf of the Country Director, such as regulatory or policy studies, Innovation or pilot projects, organizational change and improvement efforts.
  • For each initiative: Define scope, objectives, timelines, and success metrics, coordinate across teams and manage external partners or consultants, drive execution, unblock constraints, and ensure delivery of high-quality outputs

Country Execution, Governance & Leadership Support

  • Support the Country Director in driving country-level execution:
    • Co-lead OKR cycles, business reviews, monthly staff meetings, and cross-team planning
    • Draft clear options memos and internal briefs for decision-making
    • Keep leadership focused on the right conversations at the right time
  • Act as a trusted advisor and representative of the Country Director in internal forums when appropriate

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • 7+ years in strategy, People Management, Human Resource business partner - including 3+ years managing teams
  • Fluency in English, Amharic preferred
  • Experience leading cross-team workstreams or systems (e.g., performance, compliance, OKR setting)
  • Familiarity with Ethiopia labor laws and donor-facing compliance expectations
  • Financial fluency: budgets, salary modeling, interpreting performance dashboards
  • Cross-functional project management experience
  • Preferred: 2+ year experience managing Health, Safety, and Security

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Addis Ababa or Bahir Dar, Ethiopia. 

Travel requirement: 25%

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Contract Duration

2 years

Eligibility

One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

Application Deadline

1 August 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

title: Ethiopia Innovations and Growth Lead

One Acre Fund has been working with farmers in the Amhara region of Ethiopia since 2014, with a specific focus on trees since 2018. The Ethiopia program has now expanded into the South Region of Ethiopia in 2024. Our aim with the tree program is to provide not only short-term income opportunities but also long-term benefits, such as soil health improvements and erosion control, so that farmers build resilience over time.

About the Role

The Innovations & Growth Lead will be an essential part of our leadership team in one of One Acre Funds fastest-growing country programs and report directly to the Country Director. 

As an Innovations & Growth Lead, you will sit at the intersection of high-level strategy and "last-mile" delivery, shaping the strategy to plant 100 million trees and generate over $100M additional impact for 440,000 Ethiopian farmers by 2030. You will also pioneer the revenue models that will make our impact self-sustaining.

You will lead a high-performing team of innovators and M&E specialists to turn a 5-year vision into a rigorous Learning Agenda”: designing the field trials, mastering the data, and proving what works before we scale it to 440,000 households. You will ensure that every piece of data collected in the field informs our highest-level strategic decisions. If you are obsessed with evidence-based growth and love solving complex operational puzzles in the field, this is for you!.

Success is measured by your ability to reach OAF Ethiopia’s 2030 objectives. You will:

  • Support our network of 1,000+ nursery managers by improving their production and finding new ways to generate income.
  • Engineer innovative, scalable solutions to maximize income for every farmer reached, unlocking opportunities for youth and women.
  • Secure our seed supply through large-scale adoption of the best varieties and partnerships like the Jimma Research Centre.
  • Define the next frontier and move beyond existing programs to identify "whats next." You will lead the feasibility studies to transition OAF Ethiopia from a traditional NGO model to a revenue-generating organization. You will investigate the regulatory landscape and operational requirements, and research and test the most impactful agricultural practices, products, and services for our farmers.

In a single week, you could present our Learning Agenda to our Steerco, deciding which new programs (like carbon credits or market access) are ready for a pilot and which arent yet viable. You would then work with the Tree innovation team to turn raw avocado trial data into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for national expansion, before travelling to a remote nursery to troubleshoot a pilot in person, interviewing nursery managers to identify why avocado grafting success rates are lagging, and pivoting the training approach on the spot.

Responsibilities

  • Translate our strategy into action: Lead multi-year impact strategies and translate them into specific field interventions across the organization.
  • Drive the "Learning Agenda": Define annual critical questions. You will decide which new services or products enter our pipeline based on scale and ROI, then set SMART objectives. For example, explore the possibility of adding high-value trees.
  • End-to-End Trial Management:  Design multi-year impact models, oversee the full lifecycle of field trials, empower and coach the impact team to research and implement impactful activities, from hypothesis and budgeting to operational workflows and staff training to translating it into actionable recommendations.
  • Evidence-Based Decision Making: Partner with our Monitoring & Evaluation teams to analyze trial data and drive "Go/No-Go" recommendations for the Country Director. 
  • Champion the professional evolution of your direct reports, providing the coaching and clarity needed to turn high-level organizational vision into rigorous, field-level results.

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

  • A proven track record with a minimum of 7 years of experience in managing complex projects or operations, or social enterprise programs in emerging markets, e.g., in agricultural innovation, extension, research & development, marketing, product development, consulting or MEL in agriculture, public health, or education (including 3+ years in one of our countries of operation).

  • Field-First Mindset: Significant experience living and working in rural or "last-mile" settings, with a deep understanding of the associated operational challenges.
  • Experimental Design & "Piloting" Mindset: Proven ability to design and execute field trials or pilot programs. You understand how to set up a "test vs. control" environment to see if a new intervention actually drives impact, you understand KPIs and success metrics and you have the judgment to adjust as needed when challenges come.
  • Evaluation Frameworks: Analyze qualitative/quantitative field data, and turn raw results into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for leadership. A plus if experience working with Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) teams to design surveys.
  • Experience managing large teams (5-10+ team members) and delivering projects successfully.
  • English required, Amharic preferred.

Benefits
